rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obstinate man repeatedly turned the thought over, following his desire to find an accusation against the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ردد فكره وأداره تابعا لهواه لأجل الوقوع على شيء يطعن به في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He weighed possible attacks on the Qur’an within himself to decide which came closest to a plausible thing to say.
rows.anchor: أوقع تقديرا للأمور التي يطعن بها فيه وقاتيها في نفسه ليعلم أيها أقرب إلى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His thinking led others into ruin by barring faith, and brought him lasting destruction that deprived him of beneficial life in both worlds.
rows.anchor: تفكيره وتقديره قد أوقع غيره في الهلاك بمنعه من حياة الإيمان أصيب هو بما منعه من حياة نافعة في الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive form declares his ruin, curse, and expulsion in this life as an invocation certain to be answered.
rows.anchor: بانيا للمفعول قوله مخبرا وداعيا دعاء مجابا لا يمكن تخلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question expresses amazement at how he made this estimate; because it is invalid, even its manner deserves rejection.
rows.anchor: معبرا بأداة الاستفهام إشارة إلى أنه مما يتعجب منه ويسأل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbasa means he frowned and scowled, darkening his face and contracting the skin between his eyes in aversion, as though perplexed with no way to fault the Prophet’s message.
rows.anchor: قطب وجهه وكلح فتربد وجهه مع تقبض جلده ما بين العينين بكراهة شديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basara follows ʿabasa as emphasis and may suggest that he weighed and pursued the matter in thought until it took root.
rows.anchor: اتباع لعبس تأكيدا لها , وربما أفهمت أنه سبر ما قاله ووزنه بميزان الفكر

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say basara is a follow-up form to ʿabasa when used for emphasis; otherwise it also occurs independently.
rows.anchor: كذا قالوا إنها اتباع إن أريد به التأكيد وإلا فقد وردت مفردة

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus gives basara the senses of frowning, seeking a need before its time, demanding a debt before due, and beginning a thing.
rows.anchor: قال في القاموس : بسر - إذا عبس , وبسر الحاجة : طلبها في غير أوانها , وبسر الدين : تقاضاه قبل محله

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Burjan says busur is a facial expression showing sorrow in the heart.
rows.anchor: قال ابن برجان : البسور هيئة في الوجه تدل على تحزن في القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His apparent search for truth makes his persistence in falsehood especially unreasonable.
rows.anchor: فكان الإصرار معه على الباطل في غاية البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although reflection led him toward faith in the Qur’an’s soundness, he turned away from that conclusion and proudly refused to acknowledge the truth.
rows.anchor: عما أداه إليه فكره من الإيمان بسلامة المنظور فيه وعلوه عن المطاعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His conceit was extreme: he brought himself to reject the truth even though he was in great need of acknowledging it.
rows.anchor: وأوجد الكبر عن الاعتراف بالحق إيجاد من هو في غاية الرغبة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His allegation treats Muhammad’s message as only an illusory set of effects without reality, whose causes are too subtle to see.
rows.anchor: أمور تخييلية لا حقائق لها , وهي لدقتها بحيث تخفى أسبابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He made the charge after his corrupt nature led him to think it useful in worldly life, without considering God’s judgment or the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: لكونه رآه نافعا لهم في الدنيا ولم يفكر في عاقبة ذلك من جهة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuʾthar means that a listener transmits it from another; the alleged magic is said to spread powerfully and divide spouses and close relatives.
rows.anchor: من شأنه أن ينقله السامع له من غيره , فهو لقوة سحريته وإفراطها في بابها يفرق بمجرد الرواية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge is transparently false on reflection because Muhammad had never practiced magic or learned it.
rows.anchor: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم ما سحر قط ولا تعلم سحرا , فكان من ادعى ذلك علم كذبه بأدنى نظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaswara can mean a fierce lion, powerful in domination, or hunters.
rows.anchor: أي أسد شديد القسر عظيم القهر فنشبت في حبائل سقر أو صيادين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their flight is prompted by something terrifying; the image is of fleeing a lion and becoming caught in Hell’s snares or in hunters’ grasp.
rows.anchor: لا يكون إلا لسبب عظيم يتشوف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They told the Prophet they would not follow until each received an open book from heaven addressed by God to that person and commanding him to follow Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : لن نتبعك حتى تأتي كلا منا بكتاب من السماء فيه : من الله إلى فلان اتبع محمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls are many, each spread open and unobstructed for reading and taking.
rows.anchor: قراطيس مكتوبة { منشرة * } أي كثيرة جدا وكل واحد منها منشور لا مانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rejects the proposed condition: they have no genuine intention to follow, whether or not they receive these documents.
rows.anchor: ليس لهم غرض في الاتباع بوجه من الوجوه لا بهذا الشرط ولا بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their real reason for turning away is that they do not fear the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: علتهم الحقيقية في هذا الإعراض أنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a great admonition that demands following and adherence, so no one can claim there was no reminder or guide.
rows.anchor: موضع وعظ عظيم يوجب إيجابا عظيما اتباعه وعدم الانفكاك عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever wills may retain the Qur’an in the heart, understand it, and embody its teaching.
rows.anchor: فثبت في صدره وعلم معناه وتخلق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is easy in wording and meaning for its originally unlearned audience; like a fresh sea, reflection yields further meanings although no one reaches its depths.
rows.anchor: خوطب به أمة أمية لا ممارسة لها لشيء من العلوم , فسهل في لفظه ومعناه غاية السهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human choice implied here does not mean independent control: God created human powers and gave servants choice, but their acts depend on His will.
rows.anchor: وكان الله سبحانه قد خلق القوى والقدر , وجعل للعبد اختيارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one remembers the Qur’an or anything else without God’s will; human acts and the will from which they arise occur by His will.
rows.anchor: وهو صريح في أن فعل العبد من المشيئة , وما ينشأ عنها إنما هو بمشيئة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone deserves to be feared for His majesty and power and is worthy to be asked for forgiveness because of His beauty and gentleness.
rows.anchor: أي وحده { أهل التقوى } أي أن يتقوه عباده ويحذروا غضبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may instead refer to the God-fearing person, while forgiveness remains something the sinner should seek from God, especially when he fears Him.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير للمتقي { وأهل المغفرة * } أي لأن يطلب غفرانه للذنوب

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet recited this verse and relayed God’s saying: whoever fears associating another with Him, God is worthy to forgive.
rows.anchor: روى أحمد والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجه والطبراني في الأوسط والحاكم وأبو يعلى والبغوي والبزار عن أنس رضي الله عنه عن النبي

rows.speaker: الترمذي وابن عدي والطبراني
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn ʿAdi, and al-Tabarani say the report is uniquely transmitted by Sahl ibn Abi Hazim al-Qutaʿi.
rows.anchor: وقال الترمذي وابن عدي والطبراني : تفرد به سهل بن أبي حزم القطعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra’s ending returns to its opening, pairing warning with glad tidings: the sinner may return to obedience and have his lapses covered, under the commands to warn, magnify God, and shun impurity.
rows.anchor: فقد رجع آخر السورة على أولها , وانطبق مفصلها على موصلها , بضم البشارة إلى النذارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra’s aim is to show the greatness of the Prophet commanded to warn by the greatness of his Sender and God’s complete power, which disclosed knowledge to him.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على عظمة المدثر المأمور بالإنذار صلى الله عليه وسلم لعظمة مرسله سبحانه وتمام اقتداره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a great reminder through clear meanings, sweet wording, grand structure, smooth composition, and lofty aims; sincere intent and resolve disclose its hidden secrets.
rows.anchor: هذا القرآن تذكرة عظيمة لما أودعه الله من وضوح المنعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The willing person remembers the Qur’an by retaining it, knowing its meanings, and taking on its character.
rows.anchor: فحفظه وعلم معانيه وتخلق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether someone is veiled from the Qur’an or receives its disclosures and treasures depends entirely on God’s will.
rows.anchor: وإنما المانع عن ذلك مشيئة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may unveil the Qur’an’s beauties and treasures to a follower and adorn him with it, as He did with Muhammad, whose character was the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: كما كان المدثر صلى الله عليه وسلم حين كان خلقه القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Qiyāma clearly signals the next sūra’s subject; its opening oath can be read as negated or emphatic although the resurrection is already unmistakably clear.
rows.anchor: واسمها القيامة واضح في ذلك جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ruler would not leave subordinates to attack one another and act without accounting; how could the Supreme Judge leave His servants unaccountable?
rows.anchor: يدع من تحت يده يعدو بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s angels oversee people at every moment, bring death, prepare them in the barzakh for presentation, gather them back to the earth, and raise them by the trumpet blast to judgment.
rows.anchor: وكل عبيده أضعافهم من الملائكة فهم يديرون كل لحظة فيهم كؤوس المنايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people do not know this by God’s will, as the commanding soul overcomes the reproaching soul; the Prophet and chosen followers receive disclosure as the tranquil soul prevails.
rows.anchor: ولم يحجب عن علم ذلك حتى ضل عنه أكثر الخلق إلا مشيئته سبحانه بتغليب النفس الأمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, God honors His Messenger through the majestic Book; the Merciful gives creation and exposition to the guided and errant, while the Compassionate grants right speech and deeds to those under His care.
rows.anchor: شرف رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأعجز الخلق بكتابه بما له من الجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening resumes the previous sūra’s warning about the Hereafter and closes the same arc with taqwa and forgiveness as its chief means of success and remedy.
rows.anchor: ذكر سبحانه الآخرة أول سورة المدثر وخوف منها بالتعبير بالناقور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers denied the Resurrection, but Qur’anic proofs with and without oaths made it nearly self-evident; an oath cannot benefit against obstinate denial.
rows.anchor: وكان سبحانه قد أقام عليها من الأدلة من أول القرآن إلى هنا تارة مع الإقسام وأخرى مع الخلو عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La uqsim may mean that God does not swear because the matter needs no oath, or that He does swear with emphasis; both readings signal the Day’s tremendous importance.
rows.anchor: لا أوقع الإقسام أو أوقعه مؤكدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If taken as an oath, it establishes the existence of the Day or is sworn because of its existence; the Day is so exalted that nothing greater could be sworn by to answer a denier.
rows.anchor: على وجود يوم القيامة أو بسبب وجوده لأن الأمر غني فيه عن ذلك

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says negation makes the affirmation stronger: it first rebuts the denier, then asserts the oath, and the combination of denial and affirmation signals exclusivity.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع , إن الإثبات من طريق النفي آكد كأنه رد على المنكر أولا ثم أثبت القسم ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproaching soul blames its owner; when it blames sin or neglect of good it saves, but reproach for the opposite course leads to ruin, and it always reproaches.
rows.anchor: أي التي تلوم صاحبها وهي خيرة وشريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproaching soul lies between the commanding and tranquil souls, and falls under whichever predominates.
rows.anchor: وهي بين الأمارة والمطمئنة , فما غلب عليها منهما كانت في حيزه

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi describes the tranquil soul as obedient to God, the commanding soul as opposing Him and following desire, and the reproaching soul as struggling with either side sometimes prevailing.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : فالمطمئنة التي انقادت لأوامر الله , والأمارة المخالفة لها المتعبة للهوى , واللوامة هي المجاهدة

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardi says there is one human soul with varying qualities; angels occupy perfection and other animals a lower state.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام السهروردي في الباب السادس والخمسين من معارفه : وهي نفس واحدة لها صفات متغايرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is paired with the reproaching soul because humans, unlike angels and nonhuman animals, receive reward and punishment; the soul’s reproach intensifies on that Day for missed good or failure to increase it.
rows.anchor: ولهذا جمع بين القيامة وبين اللوامة , لأن الثواب والعقاب للآدمي دون الملائكة والحيوانات العجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān names the human kind because most people follow appetite and self-regard over reason, except those God protects.
rows.anchor: وأسند الفعل إلى النوع كله لأن أكثرهم كذلك لغلبة الحظوظ على العقل إلا من عصم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will gather the human bones from the earth and restore them after they have disintegrated, scattered, and decayed.
rows.anchor: قالب بدنه وعماده من الأرض فيعيدها كما كانت بعد تمزقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lightened أن fills the place of the two omitted objects of يحسب, understood as: he thinks Us not gathering them.
rows.anchor: وقد سدت المخففة مسد مفعولي ( يحسب ) المقدرين ب ( يحسبنا ) غير جامعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The citation that God encompasses and counts everything supports the preceding point that deniers’ deeds are preserved.
rows.anchor: وأحصى كل شيء عددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion has established that deeds are recorded, each person witnesses against himself and knows his own good and evil despite excuses, and the Qur’an’s exposition is a clear witness against everyone.
rows.anchor: أن أعمالهم محفوظة , وأن كل أحد على نفسه شاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla denies that people are ignorant of their ugly deeds: no one commits them unknowingly, even if he later offers excuses.
rows.anchor: نافيا لما يظن من جهلهم بقبيح أفعالهم الذي اقتضاه اعتذارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their actual motive is enduring love of the immediate world, shown by their eager pursuit of it; this love leads them to knowingly commit what they know is wrong.
rows.anchor: محبة متجددة مستمرة على تجدد الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two lives are rival co-wives: loving one necessarily prompts conduct that distances a person from the other; love of a thing blinds and deafens.
rows.anchor: فإن الآخرة والأولى ضرتان من أحب إحداهما فعل ولا بد ما يباعده عن الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s haste in recitation was corrected by the command not to rush; once forbidden, he returned to his complete, tranquil nature, by God’s directing and without strain.
rows.anchor: فحين نهيناه عن ذلك انتهى رجوعا إلى طبعه الكامل الذي لا يشوبه نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They abandon the Hereafter because they hate it, having committed acts that will harm them there.
rows.anchor: لانهم يبغضونها لارتكابهم ما يضربهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural address follows the collective meaning of human, showing that only isolated people protected by God escape blameworthy haste.
rows.anchor: وجمع الضمير وإن كان مبنى الخطاب مع الإنسان نظرا نظرا للمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses use iḥtibāk: love of the present implies hatred of the Hereafter, while leaving the Hereafter implies turning toward and taking the present.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الحب أولا دليلا على البغض ثانيا , والترك ثانيا دليلا على الإقبال والأخذ أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike their souls, the Prophet’s reproaching soul urges ever more good and prompt obedience; theirs incites attachment to fleeting worldly life and abandonment of what lasts.
rows.anchor: كما أن نفسك تحثك على الازدياد من الخبر والمبادرة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The radiant faces are blessed and comfortable, with their visible brightness showing their owners’ felicity.
rows.anchor: من النضرة بالضاد , وهي النعمة والرفاهية أي هي بهية مشرقة ظاهر عليها أثر النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed gaze is directed continually toward God’s generosity and manifestation; when the veil is lifted they see Him with their eyes, so the promise denotes actual vision.
rows.anchor: فإذا رفع الحجاب عنهم أبصروه بأعينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition إلى shows real seeing, since waiting is not construed with it; the faces stand for their owners and their gaze toward God eclipses all other looking.
rows.anchor: فإن الانتظار لا يعدى بها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين وجميع أهل السنة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, most exegetes, and all Sunnis affirm that the people of Paradise see God openly, without concealment or crowding; authentic reports compare its clarity to seeing the full moon, not its direction or likeness.
rows.anchor: كما قاله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وأكثر المفسرين وجميع أهل السنة

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali allows God to create vision in a direction or elsewhere, but says the apparent scriptural language of seeing should stand unless necessity requires abandoning it.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام حجة الإسلام الغزالي رحمه الله تعالى في كتاب المحبة من الإحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say some people in Paradise see God morning and evening, and another report says only the veil of majesty remains between them and their Lord; their disclosure and joy vary with their deeds.
rows.anchor: روي أن منهم من ينظر إلى الله بكرة وعشية , وفي خبر آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The frowning faces are intensely grim and distressed, as if sunk in grief after finding no escape when they examined their state.
rows.anchor: شديدة العبوس والكلوح والتكره لما هي فيه من الغم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāsil is more emphatic than bāsir, though it is commonly used for a brave person whose scowl intensifies in battle.
rows.anchor: والباسل أبلغ من الباسر لكنه غلب في الشجاع لاشتداد كلوحه عند العراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those faces are veiled from their Lord and directed toward forms of punishment.
rows.anchor: وتلك الوجوه عن ربها محجوبة , وإلى أنواع العذاب ناظرة
